item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Scholz’s 2024 record is mixed for 8B.9. He repeatedly managed external crises and alliance relationships in a way that preserved Germany’s strategic posture, but his domestic governing coalition broke down and institutional checks remained weak by year-end. The evidence supports short-term crisis/foreign-policy management more than durable regime stability.

**Supports 8B.9**
- **Scholz: Eskalation im Ukraine-Krieg muss vermieden werden** | Deutscher Bundestag | 4 Dec 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw49-de-regierungsbefragung-1027922)  
  Scholz said Germany would keep supporting Ukraine while avoiding escalation into a Russia-NATO war, stressed that Ukraine should not be bypassed in decisions, and framed support as a strategic line rather than improvisation. IDs: `8B.9`, `1B.8`

- **Federal Chancellor’s press conference in Kyiv** | Federal Government | 2 Dec 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-pc-kyiv-2322988)  
  Scholz reaffirmed unwavering support for Ukraine, announced further arms deliveries, and tied German influence to sustained backing and endurance. IDs: `8B.9`, `1B.8`

- **Déclaration de politique générale et sécurité** | Federal Government | 6 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/politique-generale-securite-2290990)  
  After Mannheim and flooding, Scholz framed security as a core state duty, urged people not to let fear take over, and positioned the government as the actor restoring order. IDs: `8B.9`

- **Agreement on 2025 budget and growth initiative** | Federal Government | 5 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/budget-2025-2298116)  
  Scholz turned tough coalition bargaining into a concrete 49-measure package covering infrastructure, social housing, security spending, and Ukraine support, showing resource reallocation to keep the program moving. IDs: `8B.9`, `8B.8`

- **Joint press release on evaluating Bundeswehr missions abroad** | Federal Foreign Office / Federal Ministry of Defence | 26 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom/news/2664958-2664958)  
  The government conducted its first cross-mission evaluation, found improvement needs, and recommended more realistic goals, better civilian-military coordination, and more flexible crisis options. IDs: `8B.9`, `8B.8`

- **Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040)  
  Scholz tied aid to Ukraine, welfare stabilization, and defense spending to a single growth initiative, presenting a coordinated governing program rather than fragmented crisis management. IDs: `8B.9`, `8B.8`

- **Germany will approve EU’s planned AI Act - sources** | Reuters via Investing.com | 30 Jan 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/germany-will-approve-eus-planned-ai-act--sources-3286730)  
  Reuters reported that coalition objections were resolved and Germany moved to approve the AI Act via compromise, which is evidence of managing internal resistance through negotiated policy adaptation. IDs: `8B.9`

- **Germany agrees phaseout of Huawei/ZTE components in 5G core network** | Reuters via Marketscreener | 11 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DEUTSCHE-TELEKOM-AG-444661/news/Germany-agrees-phaseout-of-Huawei-ZTE-components-in-5G-core-network-47361811/)  
  The government set a concrete timetable to remove risky components from critical infrastructure, showing strategic adjustment to protect security and long-run state influence. IDs: `8B.9`

- **Chancellor press/fact rationale on Taurus** | Federal Government | 4 Mar 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/chancelier-questions-2024-2265010)  
  Scholz justified refusing Taurus deliveries on the grounds that German soldiers should not be drawn into the war, which preserved escalation control and alliance discipline even under criticism. IDs: `8B.9`, `1B.8`

- **Rafah / IHL restraint** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040)  
  Scholz said Israel had the right to defend itself but must comply with international humanitarian law and allow aid into Gaza, which shows he used an ally relationship to press for bounded conduct rather than unconditional backing. IDs: `8B.9`

**Counters 8B.9**
- **Explainer: German coalition collapses - what comes next** | Reuters via Investing.com | 6 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936)  
  Scholz’s dismissal of Lindner collapsed the coalition and triggered political chaos, a direct sign that he failed to preserve governing durability and coalition cohesion. IDs: `8B.9`, `8B.8`

- **394 Abgeordnete sprechen Bundeskanzler Scholz nicht das Vertrauen aus** | Deutscher Bundestag | 16 Dec 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198)  
  Parliament withdrew confidence by a wide margin, confirming that Scholz ended 2024 without stable authority and that the regime’s chosen program was no longer being effectively carried by the coalition. IDs: `8B.9`

- **The Federal Intelligence Service’s powers to conduct strategic surveillance ... are unconstitutional in part** | Bundesverfassungsgericht | 8 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/EN/2024/bvg24-093.html)  
  The court found parts of the BND surveillance framework unconstitutional and said independent oversight was inadequate, which is strong structural counterevidence for clean handling of institutional resistance and control systems. IDs: `8B.9`

- **Geheimes Kanzleramtsgutachten in Cum-Ex-Affäre** | Tagesspiegel | 4 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/geheimes-kanzleramtsgutachten-in-cum-ex-affare-scholz-darf-weiter-in-deckung-bleiben-11756357.html)  
  Reporting suggested the Chancellery used a legal memo to blunt Bundestag scrutiny over the Warburg/Cum-Ex affair, which points to defensive containment rather than transparent management of institutional resistance. IDs: `8B.9`

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence that Scholz could manage external crises, especially Ukraine and Gaza, by combining restraint with continued support and alliance maintenance.
- I did not find evidence that he successfully preserved domestic governing durability through late 2024; the coalition collapse and no-confidence vote are the dominant facts.
- I also did not find a convincing source showing he had fixed the deeper institutional weaknesses exposed by the BND ruling or the Cum-Ex scrutiny problems.
